dedupe_keys.name: pitea physics informed techno economic model of hydrogen pipeline transmission and buffer storage

description: PiTEA is a physics-informed techno-economic model of hydrogen pipeline transmission and buffer provision, released with its paper as a reproducibility package. Version 1.0.0 was published on Zenodo in August 2026 by Pengfei Chen and Valerie Thomas. The Python model jointly represents pipeline hydraulics, compression, pressure-swing linepack, external buffer storage, infrastructure selection and levelised cost of transport. The package includes the model source, input data, tests of physical and accounting behaviour, experiment scripts and reference results: a 48-case cost comparison with an established hydrogen pipeline cost tool, a 30-case comparison with published diameters, and 105 service points evaluated for joint pipeline and buffer design. Documentation covers data provenance, limitations and reproducibility. Coverage is generic, not tied to a place. The code is downloadable from Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: it is packaged for reproducing one article, so costs are in constant 2023 US dollars and scenarios follow the paper. Simulation uses are sizing hydrogen transmission pipelines, compression and storage and comparing linepack with separate storage. Related records: model-lanl-phydras-hydrogen-blending-pipelines models hydrogen blending in gas pipelines.
